title: The Vela supernova remnant imaged by the VLT Survey Telescope
caption: The Vela supernova remnant, imaged by ESO's VLT Survey Telescope
credit: ESO/VPHAS+ team. Acknowledgement: Cambridge Astronomical Survey Unit

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Orange and pink clouds sweep across this view, with bright blue stars scattered in front of them. The clouds are the Vela supernova remnant, the debris left behind after a massive star died in an explosion.

When a massive star explodes, it hurls material outward at great speed. As that debris plows into the thin gas between the stars, it compresses and heats it, producing the glowing filaments. The bright blue stars are in the foreground and have nothing to do with the remnant.

The image is huge, at 554 million pixels, and was assembled as a mosaic from observations with the 268-million-pixel OmegaCAM camera on the VLT Survey Telescope at ESO's Paranal Observatory. OmegaCAM can observe through several filters, each passing light of a particular color. Four were used, shown as a combination of magenta, blue, green and red, which brings out the fine gaseous filaments in detail.

understand.summary: This mosaic comes from OmegaCAM on the VLT Survey Telescope. Four filters were used, represented as magenta, blue, green and red, though the source does not say which filter received which color.
filters: 350 nm · Ultraviolet u (VLT Survey Telescope OmegaCAM)
480 nm · Optical g (VLT Survey Telescope OmegaCAM)
625 nm · Optical r (VLT Survey Telescope OmegaCAM)
659 nm · Optical H-alpha (VLT Survey Telescope OmegaCAM)
770 nm · Infrared i (VLT Survey Telescope OmegaCAM)
understand.eye: Long exposures reveal filaments far too faint for the eye, and the colors are assigned to filters rather than showing what an eye would see.
